concept: Refine vs. Restart & The Two-Iteration Rule

surface.definition: Defects in expression or polish where the underlying architecture remains sound.
surface.test: Fixing the issue leaves the rest of the codebase and architecture intact.

structural.definition: Defects in foundational architecture, data flow, or state model.
structural.test: Fixing the issue cascades into breaking or rewriting surrounding components.
structural.action: Restart with a new prompt and revised architectural strategy.
examples: In-memory volatile store vs durable queue

two_iteration_rule: If code quality and acceptance criteria do not converge within two refinement iterations, kill the thread and restart fresh. Layering successive patches onto a structurally flawed foundation triggers quality spirals and compounding context pollution.
